overview: This Senate resolution celebrates the 154th anniversary of Arbor Day, a holiday founded in 1872 to encourage tree planting, and recognizes April 24, 2026, as Arbor Day. Its findings highlight the value of trees and community tree planting, the role of managed working forests and private forests, the use of wood in building, and the Tree City USA program for urban forestry. The resolution supports the goals of Arbor Day and encourages Americans to take part in Arbor Day activities. It is ceremonial and does not change any law. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on April 30, 2026.
for: Supporters say Arbor Day encourages communities to plant and care for trees, and recognizing it promotes good stewardship of land and forests.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending, and some may disagree with parts of its findings on forest management and carbon storage.
